statement: If every full-dimensional isotropic log-concave probability law nu on R^n satisfies Var_nu(g) <= C integral |grad g|^2 dnu for admissible locally Lipschitz g, then every full-dimensional log-concave law mu with covariance Sigma satisfies Var_mu(f) <= C integral grad f^T Sigma grad f dmu for locally Lipschitz f with finite variance and covariance-weighted energy. Conversely, take Sigma=I.
assumptions: locally Lipschitz f with finite variance and covariance-weighted Dirichlet energy
source: Elementary affine change of variables in ATTEMPT.md L0; exact target matches arXiv:2610.05474v1 definition (5), Theorem 1.1. No universal target constant is proved here.
proof: Write X=m+Sigma^(1/2)Y and g(y)=f(m+Sigma^(1/2)y). Then Y is isotropic and log-concave, Var(g(Y))=Var(f(X)), and |grad_y g|^2=grad_x f^T Sigma grad_x f almost everywhere. Apply the assumed inequality. The converse follows by Sigma=I. The same locally Lipschitz class is preserved by the invertible affine map.
remaining_gap: No universal isotropic constant has been proved here.

statement: If the maximal correlation between centered U-measurable and V-measurable L2 functions is at most rho<1, Var(f(U,V)) <= [E Var(f|U)+E Var(f|V)]/(1-rho). If conditional Euclidean-block Poincare constants are bounded by M_U,M_V a.e., C_P(U,V)<=max(M_U,M_V)/(1-rho).
assumptions: maximal correlation bound for all centered functions, not only linear correlations
conditional Poincare and slicing hypotheses for the Euclidean-gradient conclusion
M_U bounds U conditional on V; M_V bounds V conditional on U
source: Owner campaign work; elementary orthogonal-projection calculation in ATTEMPT.md L1, no novelty claimed.
proof: For P=E[.|U], Q=E[.|V] on mean-zero L2, set a=Pf,b=Qf,S=||a||^2+||b||^2. S=<f,a+b> and ||a+b||^2<=(1+rho)S imply S<=(1+rho)||f||^2. Thus conditional variances sum to 2||f||^2-S >=(1-rho)||f||^2. Integrate the conditional Poincare bounds.
remaining_gap: The uniform conditional and maximal-correlation hypotheses are not established for arbitrary isotropic log-concave laws.

statement: For every n>=2 there is an isotropic log-concave law on R^n and a unit direction e such that ess sup_Y Var(<e,X>|Y)=(n+1)(n+2)/6 and ess sup_Y C_P(law(<e,X>|Y))=2(n+1)(n+2)/pi^2, where Y is the perpendicular projection of X.
assumptions: uniform law on the explicitly normalized regular simplex
direction parallel to a simplex edge
source: Owner campaign derivation in ATTEMPT.md L2; explicit Dirichlet moments and uniform interval spectral gap.
proof: Use vertices sqrt(N(N+1))(e_i-1/N) in the sum-zero hyperplane, N=n+1. Dirichlet(1,...,1) moments give covariance I. Conditional edge coordinate is uniform on an interval of length L S, with L^2=2N(N+1), S=alpha_0+alpha_1. S approaches 1 on positive-measure sets. Interval variance is (LS)^2/12 and sharp Poincare constant (LS)^2/pi^2.
remaining_gap: This refutes a conditional-bound shortcut, not global KLS or existence of an advantageous basis.

statement: In the isotropic simplex of L2, E C_P(law(<e,X>|Y))=12/pi^2 for every n>=2, but the best B such that E Var(f(X)|Y)<=B E|partial_e f(X)|^2 for all admissible f equals 2(n+1)(n+2)/pi^2. Hence replacing a random slice constant by its mean is invalid.
assumptions: same simplex and axis as L2
locally Lipschitz functions with finite full Euclidean Dirichlet energy
source: Owner campaign proof in ATTEMPT.md L3; beta moment identity and localized first Neumann eigenfunction.
proof: S~Beta(2,n-1) has E S^2=6/[(n+1)(n+2)], giving the stated average. Slice Poincare gives upper B=ess sup c. For lower B take f=a(Y)sin(pi T/[L S(Y)]), where smooth a is supported in a positive-measure interior region S>1-delta. Its conditional variance and directional energy are a^2/2 and a^2 pi^2/(2L^2 S^2); the ratio is at least L^2(1-delta)^2/pi^2. Let delta tend to zero. Full transverse energy stays finite for each fixed support and is not discarded in global KLS.
remaining_gap: A uniform global bound must also control transverse gradient energy and dependence; no complete KLS proof here.

statement: In the simplex of L2, the edge coordinate T and its perpendicular projection Y have zero linear cross-covariance but maximal correlation at least sqrt((N-2)(7N+9)/[3(N-1)(5N+6)]), N=n+1>=3; the lower bound tends to sqrt(7/15).
assumptions: same isotropic regular simplex and edge direction as L2
maximal correlation is over all centered square-integrable functions of the separate blocks
source: Owner campaign Dirichlet-moment calculation in ATTEMPT.md L4.
proof: E[T|Y]=0. Take a=T^2-1, b=E[T^2|Y]-1. Then E[ab]=Var(b), so their squared correlation is Var(b)/Var(a). The beta moment E S^4=120/[N(N+1)(N+2)(N+3)] and uniform-slice fourth moment E[T^4|Y]=L^4 S^4/80 give Var(a)=(N-1)(5N+6)/[(N+2)(N+3)] and Var(b)=(N-2)(7N+9)/[3(N+2)(N+3)].
remaining_gap: This is a positive lower bound, not an upper maximal-correlation bound or a proof of global KLS.
